rule: Item briefs come from this mapping (zone -> skills -> tools for the job), never from 'stat combo + slot'.

core.meaning: Shared mechanics near the Origin. Everyday kit any build can wear; cheapest materials (flint, bone, hide, wool, linen).

mid.meaning: Versatile and hybrid archetypes. The working tools of the trade (copper, early bronze, specialist organic kit).

outer.meaning: Specialised archetypes past the ring-7 class node. Full professional or high-status kit (bronze, gold, ivory, inlay); matches the class unlocks.

confidence.A: attested: real find of this form in the period
confidence.Art: attested in period art or texts only; construction inferred
confidence.Adapt: attested elsewhere or for another use; adapted here (disclose)
confidence.Disp: object attested, but the function used here is disputed (disclose)
confidence.U: unconfirmed: do not generate without owner sign-off

globalAvoid: iron or steel look (grey sheen, fullers, crossguards); no chainmail, rivet-mail or plate armour
stitched modern soles, welts, heels, toe caps on any footwear
aprons, kilts, loincloths or hanging panels presented as body armour; belts drawn as faulds or tassets
forked or gnarled sticks as staffs or weapons; crystal-topped staffs
stone ball set in a metal cup as a 'stone mace' (real maceheads are drilled through and sit on a wooden haft)
invented-name items, lore epithets or compound coinages (owner rules 6-8)
medieval silhouettes: closed, crested, visored or nasal helmets; heater or kite shields; longswords; buckles with tongues
glass vials, potion bottles, lanterns, candles, coins, books, scrolls
glowing gems, energy veins, glow halos, floating crystals
pentagrams, rune bands, sigils, pseudo-text or pseudo-cuneiform
single boot or glove where a pair is the item; cropped cords or shafts; arrows shown in quivers (pipeline rule)

zones.classUnlocks: trap and mark tools, venom vials, Preparation Case pack

zones.latticeRow: Focus row (Assassin, or a wand or knife)
zones.archetypes: blink 64/34/2, mark 53/45/2, shadow clone 49/49/2, mine 45/52/3, trap 36/61/3, poison, stealth
zones.role: Hunter-trapper and poisoner, and the night scout. Evidence: Oetzi's bast net and kit (c. 3300 BC); Egyptian clap-net fowling scenes; Border Cave and Kruger Cave poison applicators; boar's-tusk helmet of the scout. Blink, phase and shadow clone have no physical analogue; the nearest real kit is disguise (animal skins) and pigment for marks.
avoid: clay fire pots or bombs as mines (no pre-Iron-Age evidence)
open: Mines have no period object. Proposal: laid clay sling shot or buried stake traps; needs an owner ruling. Clay fire pots are not attested before the Iron Age.
Blink, phase and shadow clone have no material correlate. Is the disguise kit (skins, hoods) acceptable as the visual answer?
Bronze Age arrow poison in Eurasia is not proven archaeologically; the poison container rests on southern African evidence.
Lightning spells sit here only by inference (shock support is DEX, scaling is INT). Confirm the zone before briefing their foci.
